question: Does providing the parent recommendation as one learned score offset improve cross-family ranking over the otherwise identical E148 within-state learner?
intervention: Score is existing fully trained5339-input value plus one trainable scalar when the action equals the recorded frozen-parent choice. The scalar starts at zero and can become positive or negative from fitting labels. No fixed parent margin, hand-picked relic rule or post-evaluation threshold. Parent identity comes from the available baseline policy, never the outcome.
matched_control: Reuse E148 within_state. Same full public maps, initial691841 base weights, initialization seed, family/stage/branch draws, squared within-state difference loss and2000 updates per fold. One scalar is added, giving691842 total parameters; all parameters receive the same AdamW/gradient-clip recipe.
background: E148 supplied the parent only to tie-breaking/support, and proposed202 boss skips with4 wins on1184 reached menus. This does not prove every skip wrong. The new experiment tests a learned behavioral prior rather than banning skips. Earlier frozen-readout methods used a fixed parent margin; their failures remain recorded.
gate: Same E148 screen: first_card and boss_then_card must each gain20/1536 versus parent with descriptive paired p<.025. Also compare with the immutable no-offset E148 control. No automatic natural-run policy, full fit or acceptance.
failure_rule: If no qualifying gain, reject the one-scalar prior as a sufficient remedy; do not sweep offsets or thresholds on these held outcomes.
limits: Historical-family development evidence only. Recorded first-card and boss-card scopes remain separate; no incompatible prefixes spliced, new training games, external holdout or50% acceptance. Parent-only tie-breaking still applies at equal final scores.
